bad.title: Only the answer, no problem
bad.text: Nothing says what people were trying to do, so no other fix can compete.

bad.title: It builds the search bar and stops
bad.text: The fix works, but nobody checks whether something simpler would have helped more.
bad.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

good.title: The problem, in people’s terms
good.text: People can’t find how to turn off email alerts. Any fix has to solve that.

good.title: The search bar becomes one option
good.text: It stays on the table, but it no longer limits the answer.

good.title: Three options instead of one
good.text: A “Turn off these emails” link in every email wins. It’s one click from where people already are.
good.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

bad.title: A clear goal, but no fence
bad.text: Nothing tells the agent that the layout and the button wording are off limits.

bad.title: Three changes nobody asked for
bad.text: A new layout, “Sign in” renamed to “Log in” and a “Remember me” option, each needing review.
bad.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

good.title: Non-goals name what stays put
good.text: The page layout, button wording and new options are listed, so the agent leaves them alone.

good.title: One change, the one asked for
good.text: The pull request holds only the new error message, so it’s quick to review.
good.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

bad.title: The goal stops at “can switch”
bad.text: Nothing says how fast, whether the choice lasts, or if the keyboard works.

bad.title: The agent calls it done
bad.text: It added a language menu and checked it off. The brief gives nothing to test that against.
bad.wait: Press Is it done? to see this.

bad.title: The review turns into taste
bad.text: One reviewer says it looks fine, another wants it easier to find. Neither can be settled.
bad.wait: Press Is it done? to see this.

good.title: Three checks anyone can run
good.text: Under a minute for a new user, kept after a restart, and works with the keyboard only.

good.title: One check fails, and it’s clear which
good.text: Enter doesn’t work from the keyboard, so the work goes back with a precise reason.
good.wait: Press Check against the brief to see this.

bad.title: Two words nobody can check
bad.text: Each reader pictures a different “cleaner”, and none of them is wrong by the brief.

bad.title: Three unrelated changes come back
bad.text: Coupon field gone, new colors, or the total moved up. Nothing in the brief picks between them.
bad.wait: Press Ask 3 agents to see this.

good.title: Two facts anyone can watch for
good.text: Three steps or fewer, and the total shows before card details.

good.title: Each result shows its step count
good.text: The three designs differ, but each lands at 3 steps, so all of them pass.
good.wait: Press Ask 3 agents to see this.

bad.title: No path to the design system
bad.text: The request says where the button goes, but not which tokens or component to use.

bad.title: Hard-coded red, 2px corners, Georgia
bad.text: Every value is invented, and outline:none removes the focus ring.

bad.title: Nothing like Sign out beside it
bad.text: A different red, shape and font. Press Tab and no ring shows where focus is.

good.title: Token file and Button.vue, by path
good.text: The danger variant is named, and new buttons are ruled out.

good.title: One line that reuses the component
good.text: Color, shape and focus style all come from Button.vue, not from the agent.

good.title: Same shape and ring as Sign out
good.text: Press Tab from Sign out and the same focus ring lands on Delete account.

bad.title: 4,120 files for one screen
bad.text: Plus all 38 Figma pages and the whole wiki. The agent has to guess what matters.

bad.title: Context full, request cut off
bad.text: The pile used all the room, so the end of the request never reached the agent.

bad.title: It copies screens replaced last year
bad.text: The agent picked the 2023 onboarding screens as its model, since nothing marked them as old.
bad.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

good.title: Three picks, each tied to the task
good.text: Login.vue and Profile.vue show the current layout, so there’s nothing old to copy.

good.title: 12% used, request intact
good.text: Plenty of room is left, so the whole request reaches the agent.

good.title: It follows Login.vue
good.text: Same layout, same field components and the frames’ wording, so it fits the screens next to it.
good.wait: Press Send to agent to see this.

bad.title: Every word leaves room to guess
bad.text: “Small”, “soft” and “gray” each allow many sizes, shades and positions.

bad.title: A card the words allow
bad.text: The image sits on top and the date is blue, yet nothing in the request rules that out.

good.title: One link instead of a description
good.text: The agent reads sizes and colors from the Trips / Card frame, so there’s nothing to guess.

good.title: A match for the design
good.text: Image on the left, bold title, gray date and a soft shadow, same as the frame.

bad.title: Rules pasted by hand each time
bad.text: Tokens, components and copy rules go into every request, and any paste can come up short.

bad.title: Task 3 forgot the copy rules
bad.text: Nothing warned anyone. The rules were simply missing from that one paste.
bad.wait: Press Next task three times to see this.

bad.title: The dialog falls back to OK
bad.text: “Are you sure?” with OK doesn’t say that photos will be deleted.

good.title: The rules live in CLAUDE.md
good.text: The agent reads tokens, components and copy rules every session, with nothing to paste.

good.title: Task 3 says Delete 3 photos
good.text: The button says what will happen, because the copy rules came along on their own.
good.wait: Press Next task three times to see this.

bad.title: “Everything works and is tested”
bad.text: A claim with no test run, no screenshot and no list of what was checked.

bad.title: The bug reaches people first
bad.text: The next day, a report says an empty name leaves a blank tab.

good.title: The empty-name case has a test
good.text: An empty name is refused and the old name stays, and Playwright passed it.

good.title: Three screenshots: light, dark, narrow
good.text: A glance shows the tab looks right in each, without running the app.

good.title: One check left to a person
good.text: Whether the rename hint reads well is marked as theirs to check, not as passed.

bad.title: “Feels intuitive” can’t pass or fail
bad.text: Nobody can say what to look for, so it gets waved through.

bad.title: Check has nothing to check
bad.text: No search, no result, no state to look at. It’s marked done anyway.
bad.wait: Press Check on the first line to see this.

bad.title: “It works well” covers nothing
bad.text: Works how, and for which search? No result or state is named.

good.title: Type “dark”, see Theme first
good.text: One search and one expected top result, so Playwright can test it.

good.title: It passes with evidence
good.text: Playwright found Theme first, so the line is done for a reason.
good.wait: Press Check on the first line to see this.

good.title: The judgment call stays human
good.text: A test can’t tell if the order makes sense, so a person tries a few searches.

bad.title: Only the easy case is written
bad.text: Nothing covers a failed save or several tabs, which is where people lose work.

bad.title: A failed save closes the tab
bad.text: Nobody checked this state, so the changes are gone.

good.title: A failed save keeps the tab
good.text: The criterion says the tab stays open and explains why, so someone checks it.

good.title: The tab says why it stayed
good.text: “Couldn’t save. The disk is full.” The work is still there.

good.title: A width to test: 360 px
good.text: The buttons stack and Cancel stays visible, so nobody is forced to save or lose work.

bad.text: Nothing in the pull request guards Duplicate against the next change.

bad.text: A menu clean-up drops it, and people report it three days later.
